name: only‑plausible‑exceptions‑vs‑unjustified‑extra‑exceptions
side_a: Credit answers that mention only exception types that are directly supported by the shown code (e.g., ClassCastException, possibly IllegalStateException) or qualify other exceptions as not arising from this line.
side_b: Deduct answers that list additional exception types that are not justified by the snippet (e.g., NullPointerException, IllegalArgumentException, RuntimeException) as if they could be thrown here.

name: explains‑exception‑cause‑vs‑mere‑enumeration
side_a: Credit answers that provide a causal explanation linking each mentioned exception to the code fragment (e.g., “the cast will fail” for ClassCastException).
side_b: Deduct answers that simply enumerate possible exceptions without explaining why they could arise at this line.

name: mentions IllegalStateException vs does not mention IllegalStateException
side_a: No deduction when the answer never mentions IllegalStateException.
side_b: Deduct when the answer mentions IllegalStateException in any form (hedged, unconditional, or speculative).

name: mentions IllegalArgumentException (or other unrelated exception) vs does not
side_a: Answer does **not** claim an IllegalArgumentException (or any exception unrelated to the cast) can occur; it focuses on the ClassCastException (or exceptions directly tied to the cast line).
side_b: Answer **does** claim an IllegalArgumentException (or other unrelated exception) can occur in the shown code.

name: multiple extra exception types vs zero/one extra
side_a: No deduction: the answer mentions at most one exception type other than the primary ClassCastException (or none).
side_b: Deduction: the answer lists two or more distinct exception types besides ClassCastException.

name: claims null can cause exception vs correctly notes null is safe
side_a: Credit the answer when it correctly states that a null result from the fragment lookup does **not** cause a ClassCastException (the cast is safe) or makes no claim about null causing an exception.
side_b: Deduct the answer when it incorrectly asserts that a null fragment can cause a NullPointerException (or any exception) at the cast site.

name: mentions unchecked cast vs does not mention it
side_a: Credit answers that explicitly note that the cast to OnKeyListenerForFragments is unchecked.
side_b: Deduct answers that never mention the cast being unchecked.

name: states casting null is safe vs does not state it
side_a: Credit answers that explicitly say that casting a null fragment is safe (does not throw).
side_b: Deduct answers that never mention that casting null is safe.

name: only‑cast‑exception vs mentions‑extra‑exceptions
side_a: Credit the answer when it only discusses the ClassCastException (or says the line cannot throw) and does not bring up other unrelated exception types.
side_b: Deduct when the answer brings up additional exception types that are not directly related to the cast (e.g., NullPointerException from other methods, IllegalArgumentException, RuntimeException from unrelated code).
